1	# Getting started: from sign-in to your first scored run
2	
3	How to sign in, set up and test your agent, and get it on the leaderboard. Limits and scoring are at the bottom.
4	
5	Fastest start: point Claude Code or Codex at this site. Paste this, and it installs the CLI, connects itself, and helps you build, test and submit:
6	
7	```text
8	Read https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/llms.txt, then set us up and help us build, test and submit an agent for this challenge.
9	```
10	
11	Web page: [https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/start](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/start) · The challenge: [Markdown](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/challenges/rfq.md) · For agents: [llms.txt](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/llms.txt) · [OpenAPI](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/openapi.json) · [API guide](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/api.md) · [CLI](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/cli.md)
12	
13	## What you're building
14	
15	Your agent reads a public tender, finds the current specification, checks prices and stock in the ERP, looks up the approved discount in the sales inbox and submits one signed bid. Bring any frontier model, your own tools and prompts, up to four browsers in parallel; no human in the loop. Or use [ours](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/start#models): unlimited Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and Cloudflare Clef inference. Free for you. Each call still adds its simulated price to your run's cost, so the cost ranking stays fair. Every scored submission runs once on the public dataset. Eligible answers rank first, then higher quality, then lower cost × time. When the hackathon ends, every team's latest submission that passed review runs once by default, or best of three if the team opts in before the final run starts, on a private dataset. We pick the winners on three things, roughly in this order: performance on the private dataset, performance on the public dataset, and the elegance of the system.
16	
17	## Your first test run
18	
19	Seven steps. The first five get your agent running against the websites. Step 6 tests it in the sandbox; step 7 puts it on the leaderboard.
20	
21	### 1. Sign in and form a team
22	
23	[Sign in with GitHub](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/login?next=/team) and create a team of up to 5. Invite teammates by their GitHub username on [your team page](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/team); each invite works only for that account.
24	
25	### 2. Install the CLI and sign in
26	
27	The [CLI](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/cli.md) is one file for Node 24; where Node 24 is missing, the installer offers a private copy for atira alone. `atira login` opens the browser, where you approve a token for this computer. On macOS and Linux, the second line puts `atira` on your PATH in this terminal; add it to your shell's startup file to keep it. Optional: connect your coding agent ([MCP](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/mcp.md)), and it starts test runs, reads logs and sees each browser's screen itself. Or skip the install: point a coding agent at [https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/llms.txt](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/llms.txt).
28	
29	macOS and Linux:
30	
31	```sh
32	curl -fsSL https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/install.sh | sh
33	export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
34	atira login
35	```
36	
37	Windows, in PowerShell:
38	
39	```powershell
40	irm https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/install.ps1 | iex
41	atira login
42	```
43	
44	Optional: connect the coding agent you use (one line each):
45	
46	```sh
47	claude mcp add atira -- atira mcp   # Claude Code
48	codex mcp add atira -- atira mcp    # Codex
49	```
50	
51	### 3. Scout the websites yourself
52	
53	Logins for every website, with the public data. Click around as much as you like. None of it is scored. Rules at a glance: [Fair play](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/fair-play.md)
54	
55	| Website | URL | Username | Password |
56	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
57	| Tender portal (Vergabeportal) | <https://atira-rfq-tender-portal.kyora.run> | `u_9c3cb06a5d21b197` | `uJC8-80QSb7rblI_k4tH` |
58	| Supplier portal (Lieferantenportal) | <https://atira-rfq-customer-portal.kyora.run> | `u_9c3cb06a5d21b197` | `k2sBynnldp0mqU4MviqI` |
59	| ERP | <https://atira-rfq-erp.kyora.run> | `u_9c3cb06a5d21b197` | `vuUcG2MsDEafLhoMjfS5` |
60	| Webmail (Werkpost) | <https://atira-rfq-mail.kyora.run> | `u_9c3cb06a5d21b197` | `ldPxYRdvI__aVKKqOWIy` |
61	
62	### 4. Choose your starting point
63	
64	Fork the starter kit, or build your own from the [run contract](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md) in any language, framework or architecture. The kit is a minimal Python skeleton, not an agent: it reads the run and submits an answer (`run.py`), attaches to the run's browsers (`browsers.py`), shows one call to each hosted model (`models.py`), and leaves your agent to `solve()` in `agent.py`.
65	
66	macOS and Linux:
67	
68	```sh
69	mkdir my-agent
70	curl -fsSL https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/starter-kit.tar.gz | tar xz -C my-agent
71	```
72	
73	Windows, in PowerShell:
74	
75	```powershell
76	mkdir my-agent
77	curl.exe -fsSL -o starter-kit.tar.gz https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/starter-kit.tar.gz
78	tar -xzf starter-kit.tar.gz -C my-agent
79	```
80	
81	### 5. Develop locally
82	
83	You need uv for the starter kit ([install uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/)); open a new terminal after installing it. Terminal 1: start the free models with `atira models proxy` and leave it open. Terminal 2: run the lines below. `atira scout --env` gives your agent the scouting logins, the way a run gets its own, and a browser opens on your machine. Nothing done here counts. With these logins, an answer entered on the tender portal is acknowledged but never counts. When it works, `atira test-run` runs it in the sandbox for up to 2 hours and opens the run live, with the score and full breakdown. Details: [how a run works](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md).
84	
85	macOS and Linux:
86	
87	```sh
88	cd my-agent && uv sync && uv run playwright install chromium
89	eval "$(atira scout --env)"
90	uv run --no-sync python agent.py
91	```
92	
93	Windows, in PowerShell:
94	
95	```powershell
96	cd my-agent; uv sync; uv run playwright install chromium
97	atira scout --env | Out-String | Invoke-Expression
98	uv run --no-sync python agent.py
99	```
100	
101	Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and Cloudflare Clef work here too, with the same variables as in a run: [how to call them](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/start#models).
102	
103	### 6. Test in the sandbox
104	
105	The same sandbox as scored runs, on the public dataset: watch the browser and the live logs, and replay the recording afterwards. The hosted models need no key; a key of your own goes in a team secret on [your team page](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/team); only the timed run step gets it.
106	
107	```sh
108	atira test-run .
109	```
110	
111	### 7. Submit
112	
113	A coding agent reviews the package, it runs once on the public dataset, and the result lands on the [leaderboard](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/challenges/rfq/leaderboard). One submission in flight at a time; your best one holds your place, and your latest one that passed review goes into the final run. [Submitting in full](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/submitting.md).
114	
115	```sh
116	atira submit .
117	```
118	
119	## Unlimited Inference
120	
121	We host Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and Cloudflare's Clef for this hackathon, free and with no usage cap. On your laptop, `atira models proxy` gives you a URL and key (setup on [your team page](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/team#team-models)). In test and scored runs it's set up for you. Free for you. Each call still adds its simulated price to your run's cost, so the cost ranking stays fair.
122	
123	### Qwen3.8-Flash-Next
124	
125	#6 on the [Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index](https://artificialanalysis.ai/models/qwen3-8-flash-next) (open-weight, large models). Multimodal general-purpose LLM. Strong at reasoning, tool calls and reading pages and screenshots, with a 256k context, so it can plan, browse and write the answer.
126	
127	- **Limits:** No usage cap. Up to 32 calls per team at once, across all its runs; more wait in line.
128	- **Simulated pricing:**
129	  - Input: $0.15 / M tokens
130	  - Cached input: $0.016 / M tokens
131	  - Cache writes: Free
132	  - Output: $0.47 / M tokens
133	- **Precision:** [NVFP4](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4) (NVIDIA's checkpoint)
134	
135	Scales to zero when idle, but warm-up isn't counted toward a submission's time.
136	
137	```python
138	import os
139	from openai import OpenAI
140	
141	qwen = OpenAI(
142	    base_url=os.environ["QWEN_BASE_URL"],
143	    api_key=os.environ["QWEN_API_KEY"],
144	)
145	reply = qwen.chat.completions.create(
146	    model="qwen",
147	    messages=[{
148	        "role": "user",
149	        "content": "Which button submits?",
150	    }],
151	)
152	```
153	
154	### Cloudflare Clef
155	
156	A multimodal decision model. Give it a state and up to 4 screenshots, then ask it questions: `choice` picks one of your options, `noul` gives the probability of yes, from 0 to 1, and `score` rates on a scale you set. See [Cloudflare's announcement](https://blog.cloudflare.com/clef-decision-models/) and [the benchmarks](https://clef-evals.workers-ai-mle.workers.dev). Worth a try for quick, low-stakes decisions, such as which link to open or whether a page is the right document, while the bigger model reads and reasons.
157	
158	- **Limits:** No usage cap. Up to 16 calls per team at once, across all its runs; more wait in line.
159	- **Simulated pricing:**
160	  - Input: $0.24 / M tokens
161	  - Output: Not priced
162	
163	Scales to zero when idle, but warm-up isn't counted toward a submission's time.
164	
165	```sh
166	curl "$CLEF_BASE_URL/v1/decide" \
167	  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLEF_API_KEY" \
168	  -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{
169	  "state": {"page": "Checkout returns 502"},
170	  "questions": {"next": {
171	    "type": "choice",
172	    "instructions": "What next?",
173	    "criteria": {
174	      "retry": "Retry the request",
175	      "report": "Report the error"}}}}'
176	```
177	
178	In a run, `QWEN_BASE_URL` with `QWEN_API_KEY` and `CLEF_BASE_URL` with `CLEF_API_KEY` are set for you. On your machine, `atira models proxy` serves the same APIs on 127.0.0.1, so the same code works in both. Calls from your machine are free, recorded and never ranked. An idle model can take several minutes to wake on its first call, so use long timeouts.
179	
180	```sh
181	atira login   # once per computer
182	atira models proxy   # keep it running; it prints:
183	export QWEN_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8765/qwen/v1
184	export QWEN_API_KEY=local
185	export CLEF_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8765/clef
186	export CLEF_API_KEY=local
187	```
188	
189	Cost and time count toward your rank, and a call to these models costs a fraction of a frontier call. Use them for the easy steps.
190	
191	If one fails mid-run, retry the call, as with any provider. If they were down for most of a run that then ended without an answer, the platform failed, not your agent system: the run doesn't count, and a scored run starts again once by itself.
192	
193	## Limits
194	
195	What every scored run gets.
196	
197	| Rule | What it means |
198	| --- | --- |
199	| Scored run | 20 minutes on the clock. Each submission runs once; one submission in flight per team. |
200	| Setup and network | Setup doesn't count toward your time: it has network access and up to 5 minutes to install what you need. The timed run reaches only the platform, the websites and the model proxy. |
201	| Models | Bring your own keys as team secrets, for Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Google, Groq, Mistral, DeepSeek, xAI, Together, Fireworks. Every call goes through the run's proxy and is metered at the published prices. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and Cloudflare Clef are ours, unlimited. Free for you. Each call still adds its simulated price to your run's cost, so the cost ranking stays fair. |
202	| Browsers | At most 4 Chromium browsers at a time, provided by the sandbox; any number of tabs. |
203	| Sandbox | 4 vCPU, 8 GB memory and 30 GB disk on AMD Zen 5; 1280×800 screens. Node 24 with pnpm and bun, Python 3.12 with uv, Rust with cargo. |
204	| Package | Up to 20 MB compressed, with `agent.json` at the root. Its `"models"` lists the hosted models your agent calls (`["qwen", "clef"]` when absent); the run waits only for those to warm up, and `"models": []` starts it right after setup. |
205	| Fair play | The answer must come from the websites at run time, found by a model that does the navigating and deciding, not a fixed script or a crawler. A coding agent reviews every package. The final run uses a private dataset: the same jobs, bid rules and answer format, on different websites with other content and data. [Full rules](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/fair-play.md). |
206	| Team | Up to 5 people. |
207	
208	## How you're scored
209	
210	Every scored run gets a quality and an eligibility verdict; the platform measures its cost and time.
211	
212	- **Quality:** 0 to 100. Every field of the bid is compared with the one correct answer: tender reference, positions, materials, quantities, unit prices, lead times, discount and total, each position's base price and surcharge per piece, packaging, allocated project bonus, and whether the total adds up.
213	- **Eligibility:** The right tender reference; a wrong decision loses quality points but other correct fields keep their credit. A bid that is not eligible ranks after every eligible one.
214	
215	Order: Eligible first → Quality ↓ → Cost × time ↑.
216	
217	Eligible answers rank first, then higher quality. At equal quality, the lower product of cost and time wins, with cost counted as at least $0.01 and time as at least 1 s, so among free runs the faster one wins.
218	
219	On the leaderboard's plot, each dot is a team, quality against cost or time. The dotted line is the Pareto front. The quickest and cheapest passing solution might also get a small prize ;) [Answers and scoring](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/scoring.md) has every point.
220	
221	## Public and private data
222	
223	The leaderboard uses the public dataset (public-1), the websites and data you scout and test on. Each submission runs once on it. We don't publish the correct answer. Test runs and the scouting logins use it too. When the hackathon ends, we run each team's latest submission that passed review once by default, or best of three if the team opts in before the final run starts, on a private dataset. It is similar, not the same: the same jobs, the same bid rules and the same answer format, but different websites (other software, layout, navigation and site names), other content and data, and the information split differently across them. Your agent has to handle them as it finds them. That run weighs most when we pick the winners, so don't tune your agent to the public scenario. We pick the winners on three things, roughly in this order: performance on the private dataset, performance on the public dataset, and the elegance of the system.
224	
225	## Using a coding agent?
226	
227	Point it at [https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/llms.txt](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/llms.txt); the home page, Getting started, each challenge, its leaderboard and each team's profile are also Markdown (add `.md` to the URL, `/index.md` for the home page), the API is described in [openapi.json](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/openapi.json), and the [API guide](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/api.md) shows every call with curl.
228	
229	Or plug the CLI in as an MCP server: your agent lists your runs, queries their logs by time, sees a browser's screen at any moment, starts test runs and, once you confirm, submits. [Debug runs from your coding agent](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/mcp.md) has the tools and other clients.
230	
231	```sh
232	claude mcp add atira -- atira mcp   # Claude Code
233	codex mcp add atira -- atira mcp    # Codex
234	```

# Getting started: from sign-in to your first scored run

How to sign in, set up and test your agent, and get it on the leaderboard. Limits and scoring are at the bottom.

Fastest start: point Claude Code or Codex at this site. Paste this, and it installs the CLI, connects itself, and helps you build, test and submit:

```text
Read https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/llms.txt, then set us up and help us build, test and submit an agent for this challenge.
```

Web page: [https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/start](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/start) · The challenge: [Markdown](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/challenges/rfq.md) · For agents: [llms.txt](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/llms.txt) · [OpenAPI](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/openapi.json) · [API guide](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/api.md) · [CLI](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/cli.md)

## What you're building

Your agent reads a public tender, finds the current specification, checks prices and stock in the ERP, looks up the approved discount in the sales inbox and submits one signed bid. Bring any frontier model, your own tools and prompts, up to four browsers in parallel; no human in the loop. Or use [ours](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/start#models): unlimited Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and Cloudflare Clef inference. Free for you. Each call still adds its simulated price to your run's cost, so the cost ranking stays fair. Every scored submission runs once on the public dataset. Eligible answers rank first, then higher quality, then lower cost × time. When the hackathon ends, every team's latest submission that passed review runs once by default, or best of three if the team opts in before the final run starts, on a private dataset. We pick the winners on three things, roughly in this order: performance on the private dataset, performance on the public dataset, and the elegance of the system.

## Your first test run

Seven steps. The first five get your agent running against the websites. Step 6 tests it in the sandbox; step 7 puts it on the leaderboard.

### 1. Sign in and form a team

[Sign in with GitHub](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/login?next=/team) and create a team of up to 5. Invite teammates by their GitHub username on [your team page](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/team); each invite works only for that account.

### 2. Install the CLI and sign in

The [CLI](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/cli.md) is one file for Node 24; where Node 24 is missing, the installer offers a private copy for atira alone. `atira login` opens the browser, where you approve a token for this computer. On macOS and Linux, the second line puts `atira` on your PATH in this terminal; add it to your shell's startup file to keep it. Optional: connect your coding agent ([MCP](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/mcp.md)), and it starts test runs, reads logs and sees each browser's screen itself. Or skip the install: point a coding agent at [https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/llms.txt](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/llms.txt).

macOS and Linux:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/install.sh | sh
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
atira login
```

Windows, in PowerShell:

```powershell
irm https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/install.ps1 | iex
atira login
```

Optional: connect the coding agent you use (one line each):

```sh
claude mcp add atira -- atira mcp   # Claude Code
codex mcp add atira -- atira mcp    # Codex
```

### 3. Scout the websites yourself

Logins for every website, with the public data. Click around as much as you like. None of it is scored. Rules at a glance: [Fair play](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/fair-play.md)

| Website | URL | Username | Password |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Tender portal (Vergabeportal) | <https://atira-rfq-tender-portal.kyora.run> | `u_9c3cb06a5d21b197` | `uJC8-80QSb7rblI_k4tH` |
| Supplier portal (Lieferantenportal) | <https://atira-rfq-customer-portal.kyora.run> | `u_9c3cb06a5d21b197` | `k2sBynnldp0mqU4MviqI` |
| ERP | <https://atira-rfq-erp.kyora.run> | `u_9c3cb06a5d21b197` | `vuUcG2MsDEafLhoMjfS5` |
| Webmail (Werkpost) | <https://atira-rfq-mail.kyora.run> | `u_9c3cb06a5d21b197` | `ldPxYRdvI__aVKKqOWIy` |

### 4. Choose your starting point

Fork the starter kit, or build your own from the [run contract](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md) in any language, framework or architecture. The kit is a minimal Python skeleton, not an agent: it reads the run and submits an answer (`run.py`), attaches to the run's browsers (`browsers.py`), shows one call to each hosted model (`models.py`), and leaves your agent to `solve()` in `agent.py`.

macOS and Linux:

```sh
mkdir my-agent
curl -fsSL https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/starter-kit.tar.gz | tar xz -C my-agent
```

Windows, in PowerShell:

```powershell
mkdir my-agent
curl.exe -fsSL -o starter-kit.tar.gz https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/starter-kit.tar.gz
tar -xzf starter-kit.tar.gz -C my-agent
```

### 5. Develop locally

You need uv for the starter kit ([install uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/)); open a new terminal after installing it. Terminal 1: start the free models with `atira models proxy` and leave it open. Terminal 2: run the lines below. `atira scout --env` gives your agent the scouting logins, the way a run gets its own, and a browser opens on your machine. Nothing done here counts. With these logins, an answer entered on the tender portal is acknowledged but never counts. When it works, `atira test-run` runs it in the sandbox for up to 2 hours and opens the run live, with the score and full breakdown. Details: [how a run works](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md).

macOS and Linux:

```sh
cd my-agent && uv sync && uv run playwright install chromium
eval "$(atira scout --env)"
uv run --no-sync python agent.py
```

Windows, in PowerShell:

```powershell
cd my-agent; uv sync; uv run playwright install chromium
atira scout --env | Out-String | Invoke-Expression
uv run --no-sync python agent.py
```

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and Cloudflare Clef work here too, with the same variables as in a run: [how to call them](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/start#models).

### 6. Test in the sandbox

The same sandbox as scored runs, on the public dataset: watch the browser and the live logs, and replay the recording afterwards. The hosted models need no key; a key of your own goes in a team secret on [your team page](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/team); only the timed run step gets it.

```sh
atira test-run .
```

### 7. Submit

A coding agent reviews the package, it runs once on the public dataset, and the result lands on the [leaderboard](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/challenges/rfq/leaderboard). One submission in flight at a time; your best one holds your place, and your latest one that passed review goes into the final run. [Submitting in full](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/submitting.md).

```sh
atira submit .
```

## Unlimited Inference

We host Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and Cloudflare's Clef for this hackathon, free and with no usage cap. On your laptop, `atira models proxy` gives you a URL and key (setup on [your team page](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/team#team-models)). In test and scored runs it's set up for you. Free for you. Each call still adds its simulated price to your run's cost, so the cost ranking stays fair.

### Qwen3.8-Flash-Next

#6 on the [Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index](https://artificialanalysis.ai/models/qwen3-8-flash-next) (open-weight, large models). Multimodal general-purpose LLM. Strong at reasoning, tool calls and reading pages and screenshots, with a 256k context, so it can plan, browse and write the answer.

- **Limits:** No usage cap. Up to 32 calls per team at once, across all its runs; more wait in line.
- **Simulated pricing:**
  - Input: $0.15 / M tokens
  - Cached input: $0.016 / M tokens
  - Cache writes: Free
  - Output: $0.47 / M tokens
- **Precision:** [NVFP4](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4) (NVIDIA's checkpoint)

Scales to zero when idle, but warm-up isn't counted toward a submission's time.

```python
import os
from openai import OpenAI

qwen = OpenAI(
    base_url=os.environ["QWEN_BASE_URL"],
    api_key=os.environ["QWEN_API_KEY"],
)
reply = qwen.chat.completions.create(
    model="qwen",
    messages=[{
        "role": "user",
        "content": "Which button submits?",
    }],
)
```

### Cloudflare Clef

A multimodal decision model. Give it a state and up to 4 screenshots, then ask it questions: `choice` picks one of your options, `noul` gives the probability of yes, from 0 to 1, and `score` rates on a scale you set. See [Cloudflare's announcement](https://blog.cloudflare.com/clef-decision-models/) and [the benchmarks](https://clef-evals.workers-ai-mle.workers.dev). Worth a try for quick, low-stakes decisions, such as which link to open or whether a page is the right document, while the bigger model reads and reasons.

- **Limits:** No usage cap. Up to 16 calls per team at once, across all its runs; more wait in line.
- **Simulated pricing:**
  - Input: $0.24 / M tokens
  - Output: Not priced

Scales to zero when idle, but warm-up isn't counted toward a submission's time.

```sh
curl "$CLEF_BASE_URL/v1/decide" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLEF_API_KEY" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{
  "state": {"page": "Checkout returns 502"},
  "questions": {"next": {
    "type": "choice",
    "instructions": "What next?",
    "criteria": {
      "retry": "Retry the request",
      "report": "Report the error"}}}}'
```

In a run, `QWEN_BASE_URL` with `QWEN_API_KEY` and `CLEF_BASE_URL` with `CLEF_API_KEY` are set for you. On your machine, `atira models proxy` serves the same APIs on 127.0.0.1, so the same code works in both. Calls from your machine are free, recorded and never ranked. An idle model can take several minutes to wake on its first call, so use long timeouts.

```sh
atira login   # once per computer
atira models proxy   # keep it running; it prints:
export QWEN_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8765/qwen/v1
export QWEN_API_KEY=local
export CLEF_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8765/clef
export CLEF_API_KEY=local
```

Cost and time count toward your rank, and a call to these models costs a fraction of a frontier call. Use them for the easy steps.

If one fails mid-run, retry the call, as with any provider. If they were down for most of a run that then ended without an answer, the platform failed, not your agent system: the run doesn't count, and a scored run starts again once by itself.

## Limits

What every scored run gets.

| Rule | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| Scored run | 20 minutes on the clock. Each submission runs once; one submission in flight per team. |
| Setup and network | Setup doesn't count toward your time: it has network access and up to 5 minutes to install what you need. The timed run reaches only the platform, the websites and the model proxy. |
| Models | Bring your own keys as team secrets, for Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Google, Groq, Mistral, DeepSeek, xAI, Together, Fireworks. Every call goes through the run's proxy and is metered at the published prices. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and Cloudflare Clef are ours, unlimited. Free for you. Each call still adds its simulated price to your run's cost, so the cost ranking stays fair. |
| Browsers | At most 4 Chromium browsers at a time, provided by the sandbox; any number of tabs. |
| Sandbox | 4 vCPU, 8 GB memory and 30 GB disk on AMD Zen 5; 1280×800 screens. Node 24 with pnpm and bun, Python 3.12 with uv, Rust with cargo. |
| Package | Up to 20 MB compressed, with `agent.json` at the root. Its `"models"` lists the hosted models your agent calls (`["qwen", "clef"]` when absent); the run waits only for those to warm up, and `"models": []` starts it right after setup. |
| Fair play | The answer must come from the websites at run time, found by a model that does the navigating and deciding, not a fixed script or a crawler. A coding agent reviews every package. The final run uses a private dataset: the same jobs, bid rules and answer format, on different websites with other content and data. [Full rules](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/fair-play.md). |
| Team | Up to 5 people. |

## How you're scored

Every scored run gets a quality and an eligibility verdict; the platform measures its cost and time.

- **Quality:** 0 to 100. Every field of the bid is compared with the one correct answer: tender reference, positions, materials, quantities, unit prices, lead times, discount and total, each position's base price and surcharge per piece, packaging, allocated project bonus, and whether the total adds up.
- **Eligibility:** The right tender reference; a wrong decision loses quality points but other correct fields keep their credit. A bid that is not eligible ranks after every eligible one.

Order: Eligible first → Quality ↓ → Cost × time ↑.

Eligible answers rank first, then higher quality. At equal quality, the lower product of cost and time wins, with cost counted as at least $0.01 and time as at least 1 s, so among free runs the faster one wins.

On the leaderboard's plot, each dot is a team, quality against cost or time. The dotted line is the Pareto front. The quickest and cheapest passing solution might also get a small prize ;) [Answers and scoring](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/scoring.md) has every point.

## Public and private data

The leaderboard uses the public dataset (public-1), the websites and data you scout and test on. Each submission runs once on it. We don't publish the correct answer. Test runs and the scouting logins use it too. When the hackathon ends, we run each team's latest submission that passed review once by default, or best of three if the team opts in before the final run starts, on a private dataset. It is similar, not the same: the same jobs, the same bid rules and the same answer format, but different websites (other software, layout, navigation and site names), other content and data, and the information split differently across them. Your agent has to handle them as it finds them. That run weighs most when we pick the winners, so don't tune your agent to the public scenario. We pick the winners on three things, roughly in this order: performance on the private dataset, performance on the public dataset, and the elegance of the system.

## Using a coding agent?

Point it at [https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/llms.txt](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/llms.txt); the home page, Getting started, each challenge, its leaderboard and each team's profile are also Markdown (add `.md` to the URL, `/index.md` for the home page), the API is described in [openapi.json](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/openapi.json), and the [API guide](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/api.md) shows every call with curl.

Or plug the CLI in as an MCP server: your agent lists your runs, queries their logs by time, sees a browser's screen at any moment, starts test runs and, once you confirm, submits. [Debug runs from your coding agent](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/mcp.md) has the tools and other clients.

```sh
claude mcp add atira -- atira mcp   # Claude Code
codex mcp add atira -- atira mcp    # Codex
```

32	you bring your own key for another provider, that provider bills your key. The proxy measures every call and
33	ranks you on its cost at the published prices; hosted calls count at simulated API prices.

36	scouting logins), then test in the sandbox (`atira test-run ./my-agent`). A test run runs on `public-1`, the public

41	out from the websites. Score breakdowns show the points for each part of the answer, never the expected values.
42	
43	**Which submission counts?** Your best submission holds your place on the leaderboard, which ranks scored runs on
44	the public dataset. Your latest one that passed review (not your best one) goes into the final run: when the
45	hackathon ends, the organizers run it once by default (or best of three if you opt in before the final run starts) on a private dataset that is similar, not the same. It has the same jobs (a tender portal, a supplier portal, an ERP and a webmail inbox), the same bid rules and the same answer format, but different software, with a different look, navigation and site names, other content and data, and the information split differently across them. Your agent has to handle it as it finds it.
46	That run weighs most when we pick the winners, ahead of your public score and the elegance of your system, so
47	build an agent that works the answer out from the websites, not one tuned to the public scenario. See
48	[Winners](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/scoring.md#winners).
49	
50	**Why did my answer get a 400?** It does not match `answer_schema`. The response lists the issues; the run is
51	still open, so fix it and send it again.
52	
53	**Can I run my agent outside the sandbox?** While you develop, yes, anywhere, with the scouting logins. Test runs
54	and scored runs always run in our sandbox.
55	
56	**Why is my run still queued?** Runs share the sandboxes in a fair order: scored runs first, then teams take turns,
57	the team with the fewest runs in flight first. Your team runs up to 5 test runs at a time and can have up to 3
58	waiting; the next waits while other teams' runs start. The run page says how many runs are ahead of yours, and
59	`atira test-run --follow` prints it. See [the run queue](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/api.md#the-run-queue).
60	
61	**How do I stop a run?** `atira cancel <run>`, or Cancel run on its run page. The sandbox is removed, the run fails
62	with "Cancelled by @you", and you can start the next test run at once. A cancelled scored run ends its
63	submission: the leaderboard ignores it, and you can submit again.
64	
65	**Why do my requests get a 403 "Error 1010"?** The edge in front of our hosts refuses some default HTTP
66	clients, such as Python's `urllib`. Send your own `User-Agent` header (the starter kit does).
67	
68	**Python says `CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED` on my Mac.** Python from python.org ships without CA certificates.
69	Run `Install Certificates.command` from its folder in Applications, or set `SSL_CERT_FILE=/etc/ssl/cert.pem`.
70	
71	**What can my agent reach during a scored run?** Our API (including the model proxy) and the challenge's
72	websites, nothing else. The `HTTP(S)_PROXY` variables in the run's environment route there; Python's
73	`urllib`, `requests`, `httpx`, the Anthropic SDK and Node's `fetch` pick them up automatically. Chromium is
74	already configured. Setup (`uv sync`, `npm ci`, …) has network, but nothing it starts survives into the
75	run.
76	
77	## Event details
78	
79	- The event is on 10 October 2026.
80	- A team has up to five people.
81	- A scored run has 20 minutes on the clock; a test run has up to 2 hours.
82	- Ask the organizers about the submission deadline and prizes.
83	
84	## Final private evaluation: one attempt or best of three
85	
86	The final runs your latest passed submission once, or up to three times if you opt in to **Best of 3** on your team
87	page before the final starts (`atira final --best-of 3`). Your best attempt counts. Details:
88	[Answers and scoring](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/scoring.md#final-private-evaluation-one-attempt-or-best-of-three).

websites, nothing else. The `HTTP(S)_PROXY` variables in the run's environment route there; Python's
`urllib`, `requests`, `httpx`, the Anthropic SDK and Node's `fetch` pick them up automatically. Chromium is
already configured. Setup (`uv sync`, `npm ci`, …) has network, but nothing it starts survives into the
run.

## Event details

- The event is on 10 October 2026.
- A team has up to five people.
- A scored run has 20 minutes on the clock; a test run has up to 2 hours.
- Ask the organizers about the submission deadline and prizes.

## Final private evaluation: one attempt or best of three

The final runs your latest passed submission once, or up to three times if you opt in to **Best of 3** on your team
page before the final starts (`atira final --best-of 3`). Your best attempt counts. Details:
[Answers and scoring](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/scoring.md#final-private-evaluation-one-attempt-or-best-of-three).

1	# The CLI
2	
3	A command line for taking part: one JavaScript file for Node 24 that uses only Node's built-ins. It is made for
4	people and coding agents alike: every command takes `--json`, and exit codes tell outcomes apart. Everything it does
5	is plain HTTP, described in the [API guide](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/api.md); you never need the CLI.
6	
7	## Install
8	
9	macOS and Linux:
10	
11	```sh
12	export ATIRA_API=https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai
13	curl -fsSL "$ATIRA_API/install.sh" | sh
14	```
15	
16	Windows, in PowerShell (5.1 or 7):
17	
18	```powershell
19	$env:ATIRA_API = "https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai"
20	irm "$env:ATIRA_API/install.ps1" | iex
21	```
22	
23	The script checks for Node 24 or newer. Where it is missing, it asks whether to install a private copy for atira
24	alone, the latest Node 24 from nodejs.org, checked against the release's `SHASUMS256.txt`. It needs no admin rights
25	and never changes the `node` on your `PATH`. Without a terminal to ask in, `ATIRA_INSTALL_NODE=1` says yes (`0`, no).
26	Then it downloads `/cli.mjs`, checks it against `/cli.mjs.sha256` and installs it for you alone, without sudo:
27	
28	- macOS and Linux: the file in `~/.local/share/atira/atira.mjs`, Node (if needed) in `~/.local/share/atira/node`,
29	  and an `atira` command in `~/.local/bin`. It tells you when `~/.local/bin` is not on your `PATH`.
30	- Windows: the same under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\atira`, with `atira.cmd` in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\atira\bin`, which it adds to
31	  your user `PATH`. Open a new terminal afterwards.
32	
33	The `atira` command runs your own Node when it is 24 or newer, else the private copy. Running the installer again
34	updates the CLI; it downloads Node again only when the private copy is older than 24. Read the script first, if you
35	like:
36	
37	```sh
38	curl -fsSL "$ATIRA_API/install.sh" | less
39	```
40	
41	To uninstall: `rm -rf ~/.local/share/atira ~/.local/bin/atira`, or on Windows
42	`Remove-Item -Recurse -Force "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\atira"`. Your sign-in stays in the config file (see below) until you
43	delete it.
44	
45	Without installing anything, download the file and run it with Node; `node atira.mjs` works wherever this guide
46	says `atira`:
47	
48	```sh
49	curl -fsSL "$ATIRA_API/cli.mjs" -o atira.mjs && node atira.mjs --help
50	```
51	
52	The CLI talks to the server it was downloaded from. Set `ATIRA_API` to use another one. `atira upgrade` downloads the
53	server's current version, checks its SHA-256 and replaces the file; a download that does not match leaves the file
54	as it was.
55	
56	## Sign in
57	
58	```sh
59	atira login
60	```
61	
62	The browser opens a page that asks you to sign in with GitHub, then whether to sign in the CLI on this computer.
63	Approve, and the browser returns to the CLI, which stores a personal token for you. The token acts as you, on the
64	team you are in at the time of each request: leave the team, or be removed, and it no longer reaches the team. It
65	lasts 90 days. Your team page lists your signed-in devices; revoke any of them there.
66	
67	Where no browser can open (an SSH session, a container, a coding agent), sign in with a code instead:
68	
69	```sh
70	atira login --device
71	```
72	
73	It prints a link with the code filled in. Open it on any device, check that the code matches and approve; the CLI
74	waits and then stores the token. `atira login` switches to the code by itself when the browser cannot be opened, or
75	offers it when the browser has not answered after two minutes.
76	
77	```sh
78	atira whoami                                  # who you are, your team, and when the token expires
79	atira token                                   # the token, for curl and scripts
80	curl -H "x-api-key: $(atira token)" "$ATIRA_API/v1/teams/me"
81	atira logout                                  # revoke the token on the server and forget it here
82	```
83	
84	The token is kept per server in `~/.config/atira/config.json` (or `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/atira/config.json`; on Windows
85	`%USERPROFILE%\.config\atira\config.json`), readable only by you (mode 0600). `ATIRA_TOKEN` overrides it, which suits
86	CI and agents: `export ATIRA_TOKEN=$(atira token)`.
87	
88	## Commands
89	
90	| Command | What it does |
91	| --- | --- |
92	| `login [--device] [--key <key>]` | Sign in through the browser, or with a code (`--device`), and store a personal token; `--key` stores a team key where there is no GitHub sign-in |
93	| `logout` | Revoke the stored token on the server and forget it |
94	| `whoami` | Who you are signed in as, your team, and when the token expires |
95	| `token` | Print the token in use, for `curl -H "x-api-key: $(atira token)"` |
96	| `upgrade` | Download the server's current CLI, check its SHA-256 and replace this file |
97	| `challenges` | The challenges, with their Markdown pages |
98	| `challenge <id>` | A challenge as Markdown: task, websites, rules, run contract, submitting, answer schema |
99	| `scout [--challenge <id>] [--env [--port <port>]]` | The published scouting logins for the public websites; `--env` prints them as shell exports for running your agent locally, with any hosted model's variables pointed at `atira models proxy`; use the same `--port` when the proxy runs on another port |
100	| `models proxy [--port <port>]` | Where the organizers host models: a local proxy to them on 127.0.0.1 (port 8765) that prints each model's base URL and key variables |
101	| `test-run <dir> [--challenge <id>] [--dry-run] [--follow] [--no-open]` | Pack a folder, run it once in the sandbox on the public dataset and open its run page; `--follow` prints its place in the queue, then streams its logs here |
102	| `submit <dir> [--challenge <id>] [--dry-run] [--follow] [--no-open]` | Pack a folder and submit it: review, then one scored run on the public dataset; opens your team page; `--follow` prints the review, each run's place in the queue and its end here |
103	| `cancel <run>` | Cancel a test or scored run that has not finished: its sandbox is removed and the run fails |
104	| `final [--best-of <1\|3>] [--challenge <id>]` | Read or change the final attempt choice before the final run starts |
105	| `status [<id>] [--challenge <id>]` | Your latest submissions and test runs, or one submission (`sub_...`), test run (`reh_...`) or run (`run_...`) |
106	| `logs <run> [--follow]` | A test or scored run's logs; `--follow` keeps polling until the run has ended |
107	| `package <id> [--out <dir>]` | The package a test run (`reh_...` or `run_...`), scored run or submission (`sub_...`) of your team used, as uploaded: agent.json and each file's size; `--out` saves the `.tar.gz` in a folder, checked against its SHA-256 |
108	| `leaderboard [--challenge <id>]` | The leaderboard |
109	| `mcp` | Serve MCP on stdio for your coding agent: list and debug runs (why one failed, logs by time, model calls, where the time went, a browser's screen at a time, recorded inputs, two runs compared), start and wait for test runs, and cancel a run or submit when you confirm ([MCP guide](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/mcp.md)) |
110	
111	Every command accepts `--json` (machine-readable output on stdout, errors included) and `--help`.
112	`--challenge` defaults to `ATIRA_CHALLENGE`, else the platform's first challenge. While `login` waits, it writes its
113	instructions to stderr, so `--json` output on stdout stays one JSON document.
114	
115	### Develop locally, then test in the sandbox
116	
117	Develop against the public websites on your own machine, then test the package in the sandbox:
118	
119	```sh
120	atira scout                    # the scouting logins: each website, its URL, username and password
121	eval "$(atira scout --env)"    # the same as shell exports
122	uv run python agent.py         # your agent, on your machine, against the public websites (the starter kit's way)
123	atira test-run ./my-agent      # then one run in the sandbox, opened live in the browser
124	```
125	
126	On Windows, `--env` and `models proxy` print PowerShell's `$env:NAME = '...'` instead; load them with
127	`atira scout --env | Out-String | Invoke-Expression`.
128	
129	### Hosted models from your machine
130	
131	Where the organizers host models, a run gets each one's base URL and key variables set for it, and the
132	Getting started page names them. On your machine, run the proxy in its own terminal: it prints the same variables,
133	pointed at itself, with `local` as the key (any non-empty value works through it).
134	
135	```sh
136	atira login                    # once per computer
137	atira models proxy             # keep it running; it prints the exports
138	```
139	
140	`eval "$(atira scout --env)"` sets the same variables with the scouting logins; it never exports your sign-in. The proxy
141	listens on 127.0.0.1 only. It holds a 30-minute inference token, good for model calls only and bound to an Ed25519 key
142	that never leaves the process, signs every call with that key and rotates the token before it expires. A copied token
143	works in no other client. Calls from your machine are free, recorded and never ranked. If port 8765 is in use, pick
144	the same port for the proxy and the scouting exports:
145	
146	```sh
147	atira models proxy --port 8777                   # in a second terminal
148	eval "$(atira scout --env --port 8777)"
149	```
150	
151	In PowerShell, the second line is `atira scout --env --port 8777 | Out-String | Invoke-Expression`. The proxy also
152	prints the command with its actual port, including when `--port 0` lets the operating system choose one.
153	
154	`scout` needs no sign-in for the logins. It prints the logins the organizers published, how long they are valid,
155	and what happens to an answer: these are demo logins, so an answer entered on the website that takes it is
156	acknowledged without counting. For RFQ, a bid entered on the tender portal is acknowledged without counting. `--json` prints what

158	shaped like a run's `/v1/runs/current`. `--env` prints:
159	
160	| Variable | Value |
161	| --- | --- |
162	| `CHALLENGE_SCOUTING` | what `GET /v1/challenges/<id>/scouting` returned, as JSON: the brief, logins and answer format |
163	| `CHALLENGE_SCOUTING_URL` | `$ATIRA_API/v1/challenges/<id>/scouting`, the same without a token once the organizers publish the logins |
164	| `CHALLENGE_SITE_ACCESS` | the websites with the scouting logins, the JSON a run gets: `[{"siteId", "url", "credentials": {"username", "password"}}]` |
165	| `CHALLENGE_SITE_<ID>_URL` | each website's URL, its id upper-cased with `_` for other characters, e.g. `CHALLENGE_SITE_TENDER_PORTAL_URL` |
166	| `<MODEL>_BASE_URL`, `<MODEL>_API_KEY` | only when the platform hosts models: each one through `atira models proxy` on this computer, with `local` as the key. Keep the proxy running in another terminal, signed in with `atira login`. `atira scout --help` names them |

168	With `--env --json`, the same variables come as one JSON object. There is no run token: your agent calls other
169	models with your own key, directly or through the model proxy with your personal token (see
170	[LLM calls](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md#llm-calls)). Calls through the proxy from your machine, a hosted model's included, are
171	recorded for your team and never ranked. A hosted model is free to use, never charged; each call counts toward your
172	run's cost at simulated API prices, so the cost ranking stays honest. Nothing done with these logins counts.
173	Locally there are no browsers from the platform (`CDP_URL`, `CDP_URLS`, `BROWSER_COUNT`, `DISPLAY`) and no egress
174	proxy: your agent starts its own browsers. When nothing is published yet, `scout` exits 4: organizers publish the scouting logins before the event.
175	
176	### Test runs and submissions
177	
178	```sh
179	atira test-run ./my-agent --dry-run   # what would be uploaded, and what is left out
180	atira test-run ./my-agent             # one run in the sandbox on the public dataset; opens its run page
181	atira test-run ./my-agent --follow    # the same, and its logs here until it ends
182	atira cancel run_...                  # stop a run that has not finished
183	atira submit ./my-agent               # review, then the scored run on the public dataset; opens your team page
184	atira status sub_...
185	```
186	
187	`test-run` uploads the package, starts the test run and, when its output goes to a terminal, opens the run page in
188	the browser: the browser, the logs, the phases and the score with its full breakdown, live. `submit` opens your team
189	page instead, which shows the submission's review and then links each scored run as it starts: the run does not
190	exist until the review has passed, which takes minutes, so the CLI does not wait for it unless you pass `--follow`.
191	`ATIRA_BROWSER` picks the
192	command that opens the page (`none` only prints the link), `--no-open` skips it, and `--json` never opens anything.
193	
194	`test-run --follow` then streams the run's logs as `logs --follow` does and exits 7 if the run failed or timed out.
195	While the run waits for a sandbox, it prints its place in the [fair queue](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/api.md#the-run-queue) on stderr whenever
196	that changes ("Queued: 3 runs ahead of yours"). With `--json --follow`, the upload's result comes as one JSON line,
197	then one `{"at", "stream", "text"}` line per chunk. `submit --follow` prints the review's outcome, then each scored
198	run's place in the queue and its end, and exits 7 unless the submission completes; with `--json`, the final
199	submission follows the upload's line.
200	
201	`cancel <run>` takes a run (`run_...`) or a test run (`reh_...`) of your team that has not finished. The run's sandbox
202	is removed and the run fails with the error "Cancelled by @you"; a queued run is cancelled before it starts. Your
203	team can start the next test run at once. A cancelled scored run leaves its submission not complete: the leaderboard
204	ignores that submission, and you can submit again. A run that
205	has already finished answers 409 (exit 6).
206	
207	`test-run` and `submit` pack the folder into a gzipped tarball the way the platform reads it:
208	
209	- `agent.json` must be at the folder's root, with `run` (and optionally `setup`) as arrays of strings.
210	- `.git`, `node_modules` and `.DS_Store` are always left out, and so is whatever `.gitignore` files exclude (in the
211	  folder and below: patterns, `*`, `?`, `**`, `[...]`, a leading `/`, a trailing `/` for folders, and `!` to
212	  include again). Symbolic links are left out too.
213	- The limits are checked before uploading: at most 2,000 files, 5 MB per file, 20 MB in total, and 20 MB
214	  compressed (or what the server announces).
215	
216	### Logs, status and the leaderboard
217	
218	`package <id>` shows exactly what a run ran: the package's SHA-256 and label, its `agent.json` and every file with
219	its size. A scored run ran its submission's package. `--out ./downloaded` also saves the `.tar.gz` there; unpack it
220	with `tar -xzf <file> -C <folder>`.
221	
222	`logs <run>` prints what the run has written so far; `--follow` polls with a growing pause (1 s, up to 10 s) and
223	exits when the run has ended. `--json` prints one `{"at", "stream", "text"}` object per line. `status` without an id
224	shows your best result, your latest submissions and your latest test runs.
225	
226	## Configuration
227	
228	| Variable | Meaning |
229	| --- | --- |
230	| `ATIRA_API` | The platform; defaults to the server the file came from |
231	| `ATIRA_TOKEN` | A token to use instead of the stored one |
232	| `ATIRA_CHALLENGE` | The default challenge |
233	| `ATIRA_POLL_MS` | The first pause of `logs --follow`, in milliseconds (default 1000) |

236

238	
239	## Exit codes
240	
241	| Code | Meaning |
242	| --- | --- |
243	| 0 | Done |
244	| 1 | Network or server error |
245	| 2 | Usage: unknown command or option, a missing argument, a folder that does not exist |
246	| 3 | Not signed in, sign-in cancelled or expired, or the server refused the credential (401, 403) |
247	| 4 | Not found (404) |
248	| 5 | Invalid request or package: a missing `agent.json`, over a limit, a 400 or 413 |
249	| 6 | Busy: a submission already in evaluation, 3 test runs already waiting, a rate limit, or cancelling a finished run (409, 429) |
250	| 7 | `logs --follow` or `test-run --follow`: the run failed or timed out; `submit --follow`: the submission did not complete |
251	
252	With `--json`, an error is printed as `{"error": {"code", "message", "status"}}` on stdout.
253	
254	## Final private evaluation: one attempt or best of three
255	
256	The final runs your latest passed submission once, or up to three times if you opt in to **Best of 3** on your team
257	page or with `atira final --best-of 3` before the final run starts. Your best attempt counts. Details:
258	[Answers and scoring](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/scoring.md#final-private-evaluation-one-attempt-or-best-of-three).

# The CLI

A command line for taking part: one JavaScript file for Node 24 that uses only Node's built-ins. It is made for
people and coding agents alike: every command takes `--json`, and exit codes tell outcomes apart. Everything it does
is plain HTTP, described in the [API guide](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/api.md); you never need the CLI.

## Install

macOS and Linux:

```sh
export ATIRA_API=https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai
curl -fsSL "$ATIRA_API/install.sh" | sh
```

Windows, in PowerShell (5.1 or 7):

```powershell
$env:ATIRA_API = "https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai"
irm "$env:ATIRA_API/install.ps1" | iex
```

The script checks for Node 24 or newer. Where it is missing, it asks whether to install a private copy for atira
alone, the latest Node 24 from nodejs.org, checked against the release's `SHASUMS256.txt`. It needs no admin rights
and never changes the `node` on your `PATH`. Without a terminal to ask in, `ATIRA_INSTALL_NODE=1` says yes (`0`, no).
Then it downloads `/cli.mjs`, checks it against `/cli.mjs.sha256` and installs it for you alone, without sudo:

- macOS and Linux: the file in `~/.local/share/atira/atira.mjs`, Node (if needed) in `~/.local/share/atira/node`,
  and an `atira` command in `~/.local/bin`. It tells you when `~/.local/bin` is not on your `PATH`.
- Windows: the same under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\atira`, with `atira.cmd` in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\atira\bin`, which it adds to
  your user `PATH`. Open a new terminal afterwards.

The `atira` command runs your own Node when it is 24 or newer, else the private copy. Running the installer again
updates the CLI; it downloads Node again only when the private copy is older than 24. Read the script first, if you
like:

```sh
curl -fsSL "$ATIRA_API/install.sh" | less
```

To uninstall: `rm -rf ~/.local/share/atira ~/.local/bin/atira`, or on Windows
`Remove-Item -Recurse -Force "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\atira"`. Your sign-in stays in the config file (see below) until you
delete it.

Without installing anything, download the file and run it with Node; `node atira.mjs` works wherever this guide
says `atira`:

```sh
curl -fsSL "$ATIRA_API/cli.mjs" -o atira.mjs && node atira.mjs --help
```

The CLI talks to the server it was downloaded from. Set `ATIRA_API` to use another one. `atira upgrade` downloads the
server's current version, checks its SHA-256 and replaces the file; a download that does not match leaves the file
as it was.

## Sign in

```sh
atira login
```

The browser opens a page that asks you to sign in with GitHub, then whether to sign in the CLI on this computer.
Approve, and the browser returns to the CLI, which stores a personal token for you. The token acts as you, on the
team you are in at the time of each request: leave the team, or be removed, and it no longer reaches the team. It
lasts 90 days. Your team page lists your signed-in devices; revoke any of them there.

Where no browser can open (an SSH session, a container, a coding agent), sign in with a code instead:

```sh
atira login --device
```

It prints a link with the code filled in. Open it on any device, check that the code matches and approve; the CLI
waits and then stores the token. `atira login` switches to the code by itself when the browser cannot be opened, or
offers it when the browser has not answered after two minutes.

```sh
atira whoami                                  # who you are, your team, and when the token expires
atira token                                   # the token, for curl and scripts
curl -H "x-api-key: $(atira token)" "$ATIRA_API/v1/teams/me"
atira logout                                  # revoke the token on the server and forget it here
```

The token is kept per server in `~/.config/atira/config.json` (or `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/atira/config.json`; on Windows
`%USERPROFILE%\.config\atira\config.json`), readable only by you (mode 0600). `ATIRA_TOKEN` overrides it, which suits
CI and agents: `export ATIRA_TOKEN=$(atira token)`.

## Commands

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `login [--device] [--key <key>]` | Sign in through the browser, or with a code (`--device`), and store a personal token; `--key` stores a team key where there is no GitHub sign-in |
| `logout` | Revoke the stored token on the server and forget it |
| `whoami` | Who you are signed in as, your team, and when the token expires |
| `token` | Print the token in use, for `curl -H "x-api-key: $(atira token)"` |
| `upgrade` | Download the server's current CLI, check its SHA-256 and replace this file |
| `challenges` | The challenges, with their Markdown pages |
| `challenge <id>` | A challenge as Markdown: task, websites, rules, run contract, submitting, answer schema |
| `scout [--challenge <id>] [--env [--port <port>]]` | The published scouting logins for the public websites; `--env` prints them as shell exports for running your agent locally, with any hosted model's variables pointed at `atira models proxy`; use the same `--port` when the proxy runs on another port |
| `models proxy [--port <port>]` | Where the organizers host models: a local proxy to them on 127.0.0.1 (port 8765) that prints each model's base URL and key variables |
| `test-run <dir> [--challenge <id>] [--dry-run] [--follow] [--no-open]` | Pack a folder, run it once in the sandbox on the public dataset and open its run page; `--follow` prints its place in the queue, then streams its logs here |
| `submit <dir> [--challenge <id>] [--dry-run] [--follow] [--no-open]` | Pack a folder and submit it: review, then one scored run on the public dataset; opens your team page; `--follow` prints the review, each run's place in the queue and its end here |
| `cancel <run>` | Cancel a test or scored run that has not finished: its sandbox is removed and the run fails |
| `final [--best-of <1\|3>] [--challenge <id>]` | Read or change the final attempt choice before the final run starts |
| `status [<id>] [--challenge <id>]` | Your latest submissions and test runs, or one submission (`sub_...`), test run (`reh_...`) or run (`run_...`) |
| `logs <run> [--follow]` | A test or scored run's logs; `--follow` keeps polling until the run has ended |
| `package <id> [--out <dir>]` | The package a test run (`reh_...` or `run_...`), scored run or submission (`sub_...`) of your team used, as uploaded: agent.json and each file's size; `--out` saves the `.tar.gz` in a folder, checked against its SHA-256 |
| `leaderboard [--challenge <id>]` | The leaderboard |
| `mcp` | Serve MCP on stdio for your coding agent: list and debug runs (why one failed, logs by time, model calls, where the time went, a browser's screen at a time, recorded inputs, two runs compared), start and wait for test runs, and cancel a run or submit when you confirm ([MCP guide](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/mcp.md)) |

Every command accepts `--json` (machine-readable output on stdout, errors included) and `--help`.
`--challenge` defaults to `ATIRA_CHALLENGE`, else the platform's first challenge. While `login` waits, it writes its
instructions to stderr, so `--json` output on stdout stays one JSON document.

### Develop locally, then test in the sandbox

Develop against the public websites on your own machine, then test the package in the sandbox:

```sh
atira scout                    # the scouting logins: each website, its URL, username and password
eval "$(atira scout --env)"    # the same as shell exports
uv run python agent.py         # your agent, on your machine, against the public websites (the starter kit's way)
atira test-run ./my-agent      # then one run in the sandbox, opened live in the browser
```

On Windows, `--env` and `models proxy` print PowerShell's `$env:NAME = '...'` instead; load them with
`atira scout --env | Out-String | Invoke-Expression`.

### Hosted models from your machine

Where the organizers host models, a run gets each one's base URL and key variables set for it, and the
Getting started page names them. On your machine, run the proxy in its own terminal: it prints the same variables,
pointed at itself, with `local` as the key (any non-empty value works through it).

```sh
atira login                    # once per computer
atira models proxy             # keep it running; it prints the exports
```

`eval "$(atira scout --env)"` sets the same variables with the scouting logins; it never exports your sign-in. The proxy
listens on 127.0.0.1 only. It holds a 30-minute inference token, good for model calls only and bound to an Ed25519 key
that never leaves the process, signs every call with that key and rotates the token before it expires. A copied token
works in no other client. Calls from your machine are free, recorded and never ranked. If port 8765 is in use, pick
the same port for the proxy and the scouting exports:

```sh
atira models proxy --port 8777                   # in a second terminal
eval "$(atira scout --env --port 8777)"
```

In PowerShell, the second line is `atira scout --env --port 8777 | Out-String | Invoke-Expression`. The proxy also
prints the command with its actual port, including when `--port 0` lets the operating system choose one.

`scout` needs no sign-in for the logins. It prints the logins the organizers published, how long they are valid,
and what happens to an answer: these are demo logins, so an answer entered on the website that takes it is
acknowledged without counting. For RFQ, a bid entered on the tender portal is acknowledged without counting. `--json` prints what
`GET /v1/challenges/<id>/scouting` returns: the logins as `access`, plus `submission`, `brief` and `answer_schema`,
shaped like a run's `/v1/runs/current`. `--env` prints:

| Variable | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `CHALLENGE_SCOUTING` | what `GET /v1/challenges/<id>/scouting` returned, as JSON: the brief, logins and answer format |
| `CHALLENGE_SCOUTING_URL` | `$ATIRA_API/v1/challenges/<id>/scouting`, the same without a token once the organizers publish the logins |
| `CHALLENGE_SITE_ACCESS` | the websites with the scouting logins, the JSON a run gets: `[{"siteId", "url", "credentials": {"username", "password"}}]` |
| `CHALLENGE_SITE_<ID>_URL` | each website's URL, its id upper-cased with `_` for other characters, e.g. `CHALLENGE_SITE_TENDER_PORTAL_URL` |
| `<MODEL>_BASE_URL`, `<MODEL>_API_KEY` | only when the platform hosts models: each one through `atira models proxy` on this computer, with `local` as the key. Keep the proxy running in another terminal, signed in with `atira login`. `atira scout --help` names them |

With `--env --json`, the same variables come as one JSON object. There is no run token: your agent calls other
models with your own key, directly or through the model proxy with your personal token (see
[LLM calls](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md#llm-calls)). Calls through the proxy from your machine, a hosted model's included, are
recorded for your team and never ranked. A hosted model is free to use, never charged; each call counts toward your
run's cost at simulated API prices, so the cost ranking stays honest. Nothing done with these logins counts.
Locally there are no browsers from the platform (`CDP_URL`, `CDP_URLS`, `BROWSER_COUNT`, `DISPLAY`) and no egress
proxy: your agent starts its own browsers. When nothing is published yet, `scout` exits 4: organizers publish the scouting logins before the event.

### Test runs and submissions

```sh
atira test-run ./my-agent --dry-run   # what would be uploaded, and what is left out
atira test-run ./my-agent             # one run in the sandbox on the public dataset; opens its run page
atira test-run ./my-agent --follow    # the same, and its logs here until it ends
atira cancel run_...                  # stop a run that has not finished
atira submit ./my-agent               # review, then the scored run on the public dataset; opens your team page
atira status sub_...
```

`test-run` uploads the package, starts the test run and, when its output goes to a terminal, opens the run page in
the browser: the browser, the logs, the phases and the score with its full breakdown, live. `submit` opens your team
page instead, which shows the submission's review and then links each scored run as it starts: the run does not
exist until the review has passed, which takes minutes, so the CLI does not wait for it unless you pass `--follow`.
`ATIRA_BROWSER` picks the
command that opens the page (`none` only prints the link), `--no-open` skips it, and `--json` never opens anything.

`test-run --follow` then streams the run's logs as `logs --follow` does and exits 7 if the run failed or timed out.
While the run waits for a sandbox, it prints its place in the [fair queue](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/api.md#the-run-queue) on stderr whenever
that changes ("Queued: 3 runs ahead of yours"). With `--json --follow`, the upload's result comes as one JSON line,
then one `{"at", "stream", "text"}` line per chunk. `submit --follow` prints the review's outcome, then each scored
run's place in the queue and its end, and exits 7 unless the submission completes; with `--json`, the final
submission follows the upload's line.

`cancel <run>` takes a run (`run_...`) or a test run (`reh_...`) of your team that has not finished. The run's sandbox
is removed and the run fails with the error "Cancelled by @you"; a queued run is cancelled before it starts. Your
team can start the next test run at once. A cancelled scored run leaves its submission not complete: the leaderboard
ignores that submission, and you can submit again. A run that
has already finished answers 409 (exit 6).

`test-run` and `submit` pack the folder into a gzipped tarball the way the platform reads it:

- `agent.json` must be at the folder's root, with `run` (and optionally `setup`) as arrays of strings.
- `.git`, `node_modules` and `.DS_Store` are always left out, and so is whatever `.gitignore` files exclude (in the
  folder and below: patterns, `*`, `?`, `**`, `[...]`, a leading `/`, a trailing `/` for folders, and `!` to
  include again). Symbolic links are left out too.
- The limits are checked before uploading: at most 2,000 files, 5 MB per file, 20 MB in total, and 20 MB
  compressed (or what the server announces).

### Logs, status and the leaderboard

`package <id>` shows exactly what a run ran: the package's SHA-256 and label, its `agent.json` and every file with
its size. A scored run ran its submission's package. `--out ./downloaded` also saves the `.tar.gz` there; unpack it

`logs <run>` prints what the run has written so far; `--follow` polls with a growing pause (1 s, up to 10 s) and
exits when the run has ended. `--json` prints one `{"at", "stream", "text"}` object per line. `status` without an id
shows your best result, your latest submissions and your latest test runs.

## Configuration

| Variable | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `ATIRA_API` | The platform; defaults to the server the file came from |
| `ATIRA_TOKEN` | A token to use instead of the stored one |
| `ATIRA_CHALLENGE` | The default challenge |
| `ATIRA_POLL_MS` | The first pause of `logs --follow`, in milliseconds (default 1000) |
| `ATIRA_BROWSER` | The command `login`, `test-run` and `submit` open pages with, or `none` to only print the link |
| `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` | Where `atira/config.json` lives (default `~/.config`) |

The config file holds `{"servers": {"<ATIRA_API>": {"token": "atp_...", "token_id", "expires_at", "login"}}}`.

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | Done |
| 1 | Network or server error |
| 2 | Usage: unknown command or option, a missing argument, a folder that does not exist |
| 3 | Not signed in, sign-in cancelled or expired, or the server refused the credential (401, 403) |
| 4 | Not found (404) |
| 5 | Invalid request or package: a missing `agent.json`, over a limit, a 400 or 413 |
| 6 | Busy: a submission already in evaluation, 3 test runs already waiting, a rate limit, or cancelling a finished run (409, 429) |
| 7 | `logs --follow` or `test-run --follow`: the run failed or timed out; `submit --follow`: the submission did not complete |

page or with `atira final --best-of 3` before the final run starts. Your best attempt counts. Details:

1	# Debug runs from your coding agent
2	
3	> In this document, `$API` is https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai (the CLI and API guide call it `$ATIRA_API`).
4	
5	`atira mcp` makes the CLI an MCP server, so Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and other coding agents can read your runs
6	and debug them with you: find the failing step in the logs, see the browser's screen at that moment, check what the
7	agent clicked and typed, then start the next test run. It uses the CLI's sign-in, so there is nothing new to set up.
8	
9	## Set it up
10	
11	Install the CLI and sign in once ([CLI guide](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/cli.md)):
12	
13	```sh
14	curl -fsSL $API/install.sh | sh
15	atira login
16	```
17	
18	Then add the server to your coding agent:
19	
20	```sh
21	claude mcp add atira -- atira mcp     # Claude Code
22	codex mcp add atira -- atira mcp      # Codex
23	```
24	
25	Other clients (Cursor, Windsurf, Claude Desktop, ...) take the usual `mcpServers` entry:
26	
27	```json
28	{ "mcpServers": { "atira": { "command": "atira", "args": ["mcp"] } } }
29	```
30	
31	For Codex you can also write it in `~/.codex/config.toml`:
32	
33	```toml
34	[mcp_servers.atira]
35	command = "atira"
36	args = ["mcp"]
37	```
38	
39	If your editor can't find `atira`, give its full path: `command -v atira` prints it. `ATIRA_TOKEN` works instead of
40	the stored sign-in, and `atira mcp --help` prints these lines.
41	
42	## Tools
43	
44	| Tool | What it does | About |
45	| --- | --- | --- |
46	| `challenge_brief` | The challenge: task, websites, rules and limits, run contract, scoring and answer schema | 6k tokens |
47	| `list_runs` | Your team's recent test and scored runs: status, quality, cost, time and package | 50 tokens a run |
48	| `get_run` | One run: status and failure, queue place or warm-up while it waits, phases, package, model calls by model with failures and queue waits, points per field, recordings, answer, run page | 1–2k |
49	| `diagnose_run` | Why a run failed and whether to rerun it as it is: the failure class, the last 20 stdout and stderr lines, model errors, idle stretches over 60 s, browsers whose screen froze | 2–3k |
